claims.statement: Every package places "error" first in its pytest filterwarnings so any warning not on the reviewed allowlist fails the run.

ACP's normal test command covers its flat `tests/` tree under a socket block and 10-second timeout, while Talon's normal command runs its WhatsApp bridge Node tests before a socket-blocked Python test tree with the same timeout.

Talon's `tests/integration_tests` are still covered by the normal socket-blocked test target and use in-memory channel and scripted-agent doubles to exercise host orchestration without live channel services.

The root-action tests statically compare `action.yml` inputs and emitted dcode flags with the root parser, and execute the real action run body with `uvx` and `timeout` stubs so validation, construction, timeout/exit behavior, and stdin handling are tested without launching dcode.

Talon's MCP provider loads configured servers independently, namespaces and marks their tools, reports per-server state, and serializes revision-based refreshes so an in-flight request, cancellation, or a failure has defined follow-up behavior.

Talon's MCP middleware applies only to metadata-marked tools, omits optional empty string arguments, binds and resets authorization state for the tool-call ID, sanitizes MCP protocol errors into ToolMessages, and propagates non-protocol errors.
Talon stores MCP tokens in owner-restricted, lock-protected credential files keyed by server URL digest; atomic writes preserve an existing refresh token when a refresh response omits one.

Talon local subagents run as fresh task-only graphs with explicitly attached tools, no inherited parent context, and the same MCP middleware and applicable approval policy; dynamic task attachments must be unique, known, non-delegation tools on named local agents.

dcode debug logging uses per-thread, traversal-safe files with owner-only hardening, refuses unsafe paths, removes stale tagged handlers on rotation, and reports only a genuinely installed tagged handler as the active debug log.

dcode media tests preserve user-authored placeholder-like text by tracking the span of each attached image or video display token and removing only that bound occurrence when building multimodal content.

dcode's Textual message tests use a live App test harness to verify rendered-cell pointer behavior, markdown link pointers, and streaming flush lifecycle, while also testing markup safety and credential-diff redaction.

During a cron turn, Talon runs task and remote async delegation inline rather than creating a background job; inline fan-out is semaphore-bounded, waits rather than refusing excess work, and turns timeout or failure into a generic, argument-free tool error while truncating oversized results.

The persistent cron scheduler claims a due job before running it, records run and delivery outcomes, suppresses `[SILENT]` output, emits structured lifecycle events, and continues its ticker after a failed scan; scheduled host runs are timeout-bounded and recover their interrupted graph thread before propagating timeout.

Talon serializes all work for a conversation root, uses a dedicated cron thread to prevent overlapping fires of one job, and gives host lifecycle operations cleanup guarantees: partial startup unwinds started components and shutdown attempts every component even after failures.

Background subagent results are delivered through a synthetic follow-up turn with exponential retry spacing; when a completed turn's reply is superseded or cancelled before delivery, Talon requeues exactly the result IDs that turn acknowledged, while cancelled, unknown, delivered, or deliberately suppressed results are not resurrected.

Tool-approval authority is derived from trusted channel exposure and sender identity, not request metadata; cron and synthetic background-delivery turns are unattended, so they receive no approval or authorization handler and cannot claim operator authority.

FilesystemMiddleware rejects a later write_file, edit_file, or delete call in the same assistant tool-call batch when validated paths normalize to the same path, returning a ToolMessage error before either synchronous or asynchronous backend execution; distinct or invalid paths are not rejected by this guard.

Talon validates all resumable approval interrupts before prompting: IDs must be unique and nonempty and each action batch must be a nonempty sequence of mappings; it then combines valid action batches into one operator decision, expands that decision per interrupt, cancels MCP elicitation interrupts, and auto-rejects cron or background-delivery requests.

Each DeepAgentRuntime invocation captures its selected graph and approval snapshot in context-local state before execution and resets that state afterward, so a graph or policy replacement can affect later invocations without changing an invocation already blocked on approval.

Talon's host exposes approval through textual replies and prompt-bound reactions, accepts a reaction only when its prompt and sender match the pending approval, and logs redacted stable references by default while allowing raw reaction IDs only through DEEPAGENTS_TALON_APPROVAL_LOG_RAW_IDS.
